anomalies.observed: On the Navigation Computer sheet, the reset push-button SW1 (SKRPANE010) has a +3V3 arrow wired into one of its switch pins, in addition to the NRST net NET0143 and the GND connection on the other switch pole. The equivalent reset button on the Flight Control Computer sheet, SW2, is wired only between NRST (NET0090) and GND with no +3V3 connection.
anomalies.expected: A reset push-button should only connect the MCU NRST line to GND when pressed (as SW2 does on the FCC sheet); it must not tie a supply rail into the switch. The spec's reset path is just an NRST button (the SPDT TDD01H0SB1R parts are reserved for boot-select, not reset).

evidence.quote: Navigation Computer sheet, 'Reset Switch' block: '+3V3' arrow wired to SW1 (SKRPANE010), with NET0143 to the NRST side and GND to the other side
Flight Control Computer sheet, 'Reset Switch' block: SW2 (SKRPANE010) connected only to NET0090 (NRST) and GND — no +3V3

anomalies.impact: Pressing the NAVC reset button creates a low-impedance path from the 3V3 rail to GND (a supply short that can brown-out or damage the regulator/MCUs), and the button cannot pull NRST low, so the navigation MCU cannot be hardware-reset.

parsed.summary: The board otherwise matches the specification (correct parts, rails, addresses, and the documented barometer pin-swap bug), but the NAVC reset push-button SW1 has an extra +3V3 connection that its FCC counterpart SW2 lacks, which would short the 3V3 rail to ground on button press and prevent a proper reset — the one deviation I found.
